# Jubilees Chapter 46 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 46:4 — "you thought evil... God meant it for good"

All three translators rendered this passage nearly identically, recognizing its importance. The only variation was in register.

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you thought evil against me; but God meant it for good" | Literal "thought evil" |
| LOGOS | "You intended evil against me, but God intended it for good" | "Intended" more precise than "thought evil" |
| PNEUMA | "You had bad intentions toward me — but God had good intentions through you" | Dynamic with "through you" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "intended." The Ge'ez verb is volitional and purposive, not merely cognitive. "Intended" is more precise. PNEUMA's "through you" is an interpretation not in the Ge'ez.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 46:7 — date of the sons' deaths

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "in the fiftieth year of the fiftieth jubilee" | Literal calendrical note |
| LOGOS | "in the fiftieth year of the fiftieth jubilee" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "Jubilees dates this to the fiftieth year of the fiftieth jubilee" | Editorial insertion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS. PNEUMA's "Jubilees dates this to..." is a translator's note, not a translation. The calendrical note is part of the text and should be rendered as narrative, not commentary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.
